text:
Marcus Reed: perf baseline numbers are in for the new frag + burst scenarios. tl;dr: worst tail spikes line up w/ (1) mixed ctx lengths + (2) bursty arrivals + (3) multi-tenant pool.

Marcus Reed: benchmark-lab run + artifacts: https://github.com/redwood/benchmark-lab/actions/runs/7812239912 (commit `4b7c2a1`)  
raw tables: s3://redwood-benchmark-artifacts/kv-frag/2025-02-13/run-7812239912/

Marcus Reed: quick summary (A100-80G, runtime 2.31.0, compaction OFF, current allocator):
```
Scenario                           Fragm ratio p95(ms) p99(ms) alloc_fail/s notes
burst_mix_len_15s (hosted)         0.41       128     690     0.12         big spikes ~ every 2-3 bursts
burst_mix_len_15s + prefix_cache   0.47       132     910     0.18         worse (!), eviction churn
steady_uniform_2k                  0.08       96      140     0.00         stable
steady_longctx_16k                 0.19       140     260     0.01         ok-ish, but higher OOM risk
multi_tenant_4t (tiered SLAs)      0.44       155     980     0.21         starvation-y pattern in low tier
prefill_decode_interleave (real)   0.36       120     540     0.09         similar to prod traces
```

Rina Kobayashi: nice. for the “burst_mix_len_15s” config, what’s the length distribution? still 60% 2-4k / 30% 8-12k / 10% 16k?

Marcus Reed: yup. and arrivals are poisson w/ bursts (8x) every 15s. each burst lasts ~2s. concurrency target 96.

Omar El-Sayed: the prefix_cache case being worse is consistent w/ our suspicion: we’re pinning hot prefixes, then doing lots of small alloc/free for decode blocks around them → holes everywhere.

Samir Qureshi: do we have a time series for fragmentation ratio + alloc failures? want to see if failures precede the p99 spikes or happen during.

Marcus Reed: yep. in the artifact there’s `frag_timeseries.csv` + `latency_timeseries.csv`. eyeballing: fragmentation ramps up after each burst, then allocator failures spike *right before* the p99 cliff.

Hiro Tanaka: any GPU mem copy spikes / stream sync markers in the traces? or is this purely allocator search/metadata overhead?

Yuki Sato: I grabbed an nsight snapshot for the worst window (attached in the artifact). it’s mostly host-side allocator time + extra cudaMalloc retries. kernels look same; no new big memcpy.

Noah Patel: that lines up w/ what we saw in prod incident. important: the “multi_tenant_4t” case is nasty. does the p99 come from the low tier getting shoved into the worst-fit holes?

Marcus Reed: kind of. low tier has more evictions (expected), but the allocator is scanning longer free lists and thrashing. once it hits alloc failure, scheduler backpressure kicks in and latency stacks for everyone.

Sofia Ivanova: can you paste the top offenders by request class? I want to map to scheduling policy.

Marcus Reed: from `class_breakdown.md`:
- tier=gold, ctx<=4k: p99 ~ 180ms (fine)
- tier=silver, mixed: p99 ~ 620ms (bad)
- tier=bronze, longctx: p99 ~ 1.4s (terrible), plus a lot of retries

Kira Volkov: do we have a regression gate proposal from these baselines? like “frag ratio < X” or “alloc_fail/s < Y” as release blocker?

Rina Kobayashi: +1. for perf-canary we probably want a composite gate: p99 + alloc_fail + frag ratio. frag ratio alone might drift but not always hit latency.

Omar El-Sayed: suggestion (rough):
- alloc_fail/s > 0.05 for >5m in burst_mix → fail
- p99 > baseline * 1.15 → fail
- frag ratio > 0.35 sustained → warn (not necessarily fail)

Hiro Tanaka: agree. also capture “allocator scan time” metric if we can. p99 spikes look like a CPU-side stall not GPU.

Samir Qureshi: Marcus, any scenario where fragmentation ratio is high but p99 stays ok? (to test the gate idea)

Marcus Reed: steady_longctx_16k sometimes hits frag ~0.28 but p99 stays <300ms. it’s not the same churn pattern.

Noah Patel: ok so churn + burst is the trigger. that’s exactly where compaction should help.

Rina Kobayashi: can we add a smaller “micro-burst” scenario too? prod also has 2-3x spikes from retries, not just 8x.

Marcus Reed: yep. I can add `burst_mix_len_5s_3x` to the suite. will push a PR in benchmark-lab later today.

Kira Volkov: also: let’s make sure the canary scenario includes prefix_cache enabled, since it’s worse. otherwise we’ll miss the failure mode.

Omar El-Sayed: +1. that’s the one I’m optimizing for.

Marcus Reed: action items:
- I’ll post a short writeup in confluence w/ these baseline numbers + which mixes trigger worst fragmentation.
- Rina: you’ll update perf-canary proposal w/ composite gates.
- Omar/Samir: use the burst+prefix case as the primary repro for allocator/compaction testing.

Marcus Reed: (reactions) :thumbsup: :chart_with_upwards_trend:
